stories.title: Two AI companies reveal ‘Earth-shattering’ solutions to major maths problem
stories.summary: Two AI companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, independently released proofs for the VP versus VNP problem, a significant mathematical challenge related to P versus NP. Anthropic's Claude model reportedly generated its proof and formalization, which has not yet been human-verified. This development is considered a major step in understanding computational problem difficulty.
stories.finding: Two AI companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, independently released proofs for the VP versus VNP problem, a significant mathematical challenge related to P versus NP. Anthropic's Claude model reportedly generated its proof and formalization, which has not yet been human-verified. This development is considered a major step in understanding computational problem difficulty.
stories.significance: The results show that certain problem classes are inherently difficult to solve and provide progress toward tackling the major unsolved P versus NP computational puzzle.
stories.caveat: Anthropic noted that no human mathematician has verified the proof, and experts indicate further time is needed to examine the findings and determine whether they can generalise toward P versus NP.

stories.title: The mystery of sub-Neptunes – the planets we thought shouldn’t exist
stories.summary: Astronomers are using the James Webb Space Telescope to study sub-Neptunes, a common exoplanet type not found in our solar system, to understand their composition and formation. Recent observations suggest some may be "Hycean" worlds with liquid water, while others could be "soot worlds" or have magma oceans, challenging previous assumptions about planetary development.
stories.finding: Astronomers are using the James Webb Space Telescope to study sub-Neptunes, a common exoplanet type not found in our solar system, to understand their composition and formation. Recent observations suggest some may be "Hycean" worlds with liquid water, while others could be "soot worlds" or have magma oceans, challenging previous assumptions about planetary development.
stories.significance: Understanding these prevalent exoplanets could reshape models of planetary formation and expand search criteria for potentially habitable worlds beyond our solar system.
stories.caveat: Atmospheric interpretations remain actively debated, as signals such as dimethyl sulphide or missing ammonia may be explained by magma ocean chemistry, mini-gas giant structures, or other molecules.

inputFacts.finding: Sub-Neptunes, planets sized between Earth and Neptune, make up about half of confirmed exoplanets with a known radius despite not being predicted by traditional solar system planet formation models.

stories.title: Math’s holy grail, the Riemann hypothesis, appears solved with AI’s help
stories.summary: A mathematician, working with Anthropic's AI tool Claude, appears to have solved the Riemann hypothesis, a long-standing mathematical puzzle concerning prime numbers. Independent mathematicians have confirmed the result, which could have wide implications across various fields of mathematics. The proof is currently 250,000 pages of complex math.
stories.finding: A mathematician, working with Anthropic's AI tool Claude, appears to have solved the Riemann hypothesis, a long-standing mathematical puzzle concerning prime numbers. Independent mathematicians have confirmed the result, which could have wide implications across various fields of mathematics. The proof is currently 250,000 pages of complex math.
stories.significance: Resolving this century-old mathematical problem clarifies the distribution and secrets of prime numbers, underpinning numerous related mathematical statements.
stories.caveat: The dense proof spans 250,000 pages that mathematicians must still translate into human-comprehensible form, and critics question whether humans can confirm it with full certainty.

stories.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
stories.summary: A new, more precise satellite laser ranging system, developed by NASA, officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, in October 2026. This next-generation system fires laser pulses thousands of times per second and uses sensors that detect single photons, improving satellite tracking and the accuracy of Earth observation data, particularly for polar-orbiting satellites.
stories.finding: A new, more precise satellite laser ranging system, developed by NASA, officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, in October 2026. This next-generation system fires laser pulses thousands of times per second and uses sensors that detect single photons, improving satellite tracking and the accuracy of Earth observation data, particularly for polar-orbiting satellites.
stories.significance: As the northernmost facility of its kind, the system improves global network distribution, tracks polar-orbiting satellites almost every orbit, and refines the terrestrial reference frame.
stories.caveat: The remote site is next to a bird sanctuary, imposing environmental access restrictions that require remote operation during migratory bird breeding seasons.
